records.title: One tenant can reserve the entire crawler pool
records.evidence: The renamed `claim_dispatch_candidates` applies its tenant-rank predicate only when `tenant_concurrency_limit` is non-None. Its reconciliation caller passes `Settings.crawl_job_tenant_concurrency_limit`, whose new default is None, while this PR retires the prior tenant limit. The added admission test confirms that under the default tenant A claims every global slot and tenant B remains pending until an A crawl terminates.
records.impact: One tenant's long-running crawls can still prevent every other tenant from starting work for up to the configured crawl duration.
records.smallest_fix: Give the new tenant admission limit a finite effective default that preserves the previous per-tenant ceiling, while retaining an explicit deployment override. Add an admission test where tenant A reaches that cap with global capacity available and tenant B is admitted before any A run terminates.

records.title: One tenant can still reserve the entire crawl pool
records.evidence: `claim_dispatch_candidates` applies `tenant_concurrency_limit` only when it is non-None. `reconcile_crawl_work` passes `Settings.crawl_job_tenant_concurrency_limit`, whose new default is None, while this PR retires the previous tenant limit. The added admission test confirms that under the default a first tenant claims every global slot and a later tenant remains pending until one of those crawls terminates.
records.impact: A tenant that submits enough long crawls can occupy the entire crawler pool for up to a crawl duration, delaying every other tenant even though the prior default reserved capacity per tenant.
records.smallest_fix: Give `crawl_job_tenant_concurrency_limit` a finite effective default that preserves the previous per-tenant ceiling (bounded by the global capacity), while keeping an explicit override for installations that want another value. Add an admission test where tenant A has enough pending runs to fill the pool and tenant B still receives a slot before any A run terminates.

records.title: The crawler rejects media types it is designed to fetch
records.evidence: The new crawler sets every request to `Accept: text/html,application/json`. `_load_robots`, `_sitemap_urls`, and `_download_file` all use that session without an Accept override. A content-negotiating origin can therefore return 406 for text/plain robots (which this code treats as no policy) and for XML sitemaps or document responses (which become crawl failures).
records.impact: On origins that enforce content negotiation, `obey_robots` can fail open and sitemap or linked-document ingestion can fail even though those resource types are supported by the crawler.
records.smallest_fix: Advertise the actual crawler contract in the shared header—for example HTML/JSON/XML plus a `*/*` fallback, matching the previous general-purpose crawler behavior. Add an engine-level HTTP test whose robots, sitemap, and document handlers return 406 unless their media type is acceptable, then verify the robots rule is enforced and the sitemap/document paths are consumed.
